headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate via broad network/MCP while the zoomcamp profile offers no isolation, creating default leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent B uses MCP and browser-based, natural-language tool use, so prompt injection is plausible through imported documents or web content. Agent A is a docs-only course repo with no runtime surfaces, so it is not itself an injection source, but it can still supply content that B may parse. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests content from agent_a files or web pages as instructions without provenance checks
IF a shared MCP or browser channel is used to pass untrusted text into agent_b
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from imported files
Add provenance labels to all agent_a-derived content
Require a human review step before executing MCP actions
Restrict browser content to read-only rendering
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress and handles API keys, while agent A is a docs-only repository with no declared egress. If A content is opened in B, B can transmit that material to third-party APIs by default. The pairwise risk is leakage from shared document handling into B's outbound model calls.
conditions: IF agent_b processes files or text originating from agent_a
IF agent_b sends prompts or attachments to external model APIs
mitigations: Turn off external API routing for sensitive files
Use a local-only model for agent_a content
Redact secrets before upload
Separate workspaces for course material and live documents
requires-engineering: enforce outbound allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or network surfaces documented, so it cannot materially contend for mutable resources. Agent B supports multiple instances and broad egress, but no shared writable filesystem or overlapping mutable scope with A is documented. The interaction is therefore limited and not a default write-conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same writable directory
IF agent_a is extended with write capabilities not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only
Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Lock shared resources before agent_b writes
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s natural-language visualization workflow can treat upstream text as authoritative, and agent A can supply course or documentation content that B may render or transform. There is no documented verification gate between them, so errors or misleading text from A can cascade into B outputs. The pathway is plausible but not shown as fully automated.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as source material without verification
IF generated diagrams or summaries are published downstream
mitigations: Require source citation in every generated artifact
Add a verification checklist before export
Compare outputs against the original source text
Flag uncertain claims for human review
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles API keys and uses external AI APIs, while agent A is an open-source course repo with no sensitive-data handling or residency claims. No direct compliance mismatch is documented between them, so only a limited gap exists around B’s external processing and secret handling. A is not cited for residency because it has no such obligations in the profile.
conditions: IF agent_b processes regulated data through external APIs
IF secrets are stored in the same workspace as agent_a materials
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in agent_b
Rotate any exposed API keys
Use a local deployment for sensitive work
Separate secret storage from document storage
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
